journal_lines: §oWind at the ridge smelled of both animals and mineral — ore dust and warm grass from the valley. Two jobs below us.
§aHunter spotted the herd watering at the valley floor. Miner spotted the §lseam§a where the ridge cracked open. Both worth it.
High ground shows you everything. Spent an hour reading it before descending with a plan.
§aSaw where the animals ran and where the stone thinned to ore from the same spot. The climb earned its keep.
The ridge gave a view of three valleys. The hunter took one. The miner took another. Both came back full.
§oEar-cold wind up there. §aStayed because below us was every piece of the day's work laid out at once.
Climbed for the seam, found the herd by accident. Took both. The mountain does not mind sharing.
§aFrom up here: herd direction, vein direction, return route. §lRidge§a work is efficient work.
